issue.title: [testgap] Add test SAI versoin for new legacy-th image

failure.body:
## Test gap

A new SONiC image type — `legacy-th` — is introduced starting from build `20251110`. It is used by the Arista 7060CX (Tomahawk) family, which keeps an older BRCM SAI paired with the latest OCP SAI header, while other HwSKUs continue to use the standard build.

Today there is no automated test coverage for this new image type. In particular, there is nothing that verifies a built `legacy-th` image actually ships the expected BRCM SAI and OCP SAI versions for the 7060CX HwSKUs. A SAI version regression on the `legacy-th` image (wrong BRCM SAI build, wrong OCP SAI header) can land on master and reach test/production without being caught.

## Affected coverage

- No platform test runs `bcmcmd bsv` on a 7060CX DUT and asserts the parsed BRCM SAI / OCP SAI versions against the `legacy-th` baseline.
- A monolithic single-version check across all HwSKUs would either spuriously fail on 7060CX (because `legacy-th` intentionally lags BRCM SAI) or silently pass when a real regression slips through on other platforms — so the baseline must be expressed per image type.

## Expected coverage

A platform test that, for a Broadcom DUT on a release build `>= 20251110`:

1. Resolves the HwSKU to an image type (e.g., `Arista-7060CX-32S-C32` → `legacy-th`).
2. Looks up the expected BRCM SAI / OCP SAI versions for that image type.
3. Runs `bcmcmd bsv` on the DUT and parses BRCM SAI / OCP SAI / SDK from the output.
4. Asserts BRCM SAI matches `major.minor.patch` and `build >= baseline`.
5. Asserts OCP SAI header `>= minimum`.
6. Cleanly skips for non-Broadcom ASICs, non-release builds, or HwSKUs not yet in the per-image-type mapping (fail-closed: unknown HwSKU never breaks CI).

## Why this matters

- Catches `legacy-th` SAI version regressions early, before they reach production fleets running 7060CX.
- Mapping-driven design so adding the next image type (or another HwSKU under `legacy-th`) is a few-line config change with no test-logic edit.

## Suggested fix

Add `tests/platform_tests/test_sai_ocp_version.py` with two mapping-driven constants:
- `IMAGE_TYPE_VERSIONS` — expected BRCM SAI / OCP SAI versions per image type (starts with `legacy-th`).
- `HWSKU_IMAGE_TYPE_MAP` — supported HwSKU → image type mapping (starts with the Arista 7060CX family).

Implementation in progress at #25035.

resolution.title: [platform_tests] Add test_sai_ocp_version: verify BRCM SAI / OCP SAI version baseline per image type
resolution.description:
### Description of PR

Summary:
Adds `tests/platform_tests/test_sai_ocp_version.py` — a new platform test that verifies the BRCM SAI / OCP SAI version baseline on the DUT against an expected version-per-image-type matrix.

Starting from SONiC build `20251110`, different HwSKUs run different target image types (e.g., `legacy-th` for the Arista 7060CX family), each requiring specific BRCM SAI and OCP SAI versions. This test:

1. Skips if the SONiC build date is before `20251110`
2. Skips if the ASIC vendor is not Broadcom
3. Skips if the DUT HwSKU is not present in `HWSKU_IMAGE_TYPE_MAP`
4. Runs `bcmcmd bsv` and parses BRCM SAI / OCP SAI / SDK versions
5. Asserts BRCM SAI same `major.minor.patch` and `build >= baseline`; OCP SAI header `>= minimum`

The version table (`IMAGE_TYPE_VERSIONS`) and the HwSKU mapping (`HWSKU_IMAGE_TYPE_MAP`) are the only two places to edit as the support matrix evolves — adding a new HwSKU or image type is a few-line change with no test-logic edit required.

Testgap: #25036
Fixes #25036

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [x] New Test case
    - [x] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [ ] Test case improvement

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
Catch SAI version regressions early on supported HwSKUs after the `20251110` image-type split. The previous monolithic SAI version assumption no longer holds — Arista 7060CX (Tomahawk) now ships with an older BRCM SAI paired with the latest OCP SAI header (the `legacy-th` image type), while other HwSKUs use the standard build. A single hard-coded check across all platforms would either spuriously fail on 7060CX or silently pass when a real regression slips through on other platforms.

This PR closes the testgap tracked in #25036 — "Add test coverage for new legacy-th image".

#### How did you do it?
Mapping-driven design:
- `IMAGE_TYPE_VERSIONS` — per-image-type expected version constants (BRCM SAI baseline, OCP SAI minimum)
- `HWSKU_IMAGE_TYPE_MAP` — maps each supported HwSKU to its image type
- Test resolves DUT HwSKU → image type → expected versions, then parses `bcmcmd bsv` and compares

Behavior is fail-closed: any HwSKU NOT in `HWSKU_IMAGE_TYPE_MAP` causes a `pytest.skip`, so unknown HwSKUs never break CI.

#### How did you verify/test it?
Cherry-picked the same content from the internal sonic-mgmt-int branch `dev/xuliping/20260602_internal_sai_check` (commit `cdedfd937e`) — the version was validated against `bcmcmd bsv` output on Arista 7060CX testbeds.

#### Any platform specific information?
Broadcom-only — the test uses `bcmcmd bsv` which exists only on Broadcom ASICs. Cleanly skips on Mellanox / Cisco / Nokia / others via the ASIC-vendor gate.

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?
`pytest.mark.topology('any')` and `pytest.mark.device_type('physical')` — runs on any topology with a physical Broadcom DUT.

### Documentation
N/A — single-file test, no Wiki page required.
